# Memories: My Story — Extended Agent Index

## Product identity

Memories: My Story is a private Living Memory Archive. The core unit is a Living Memory: a photograph preserved together with the authentic human voice and story that give it meaning, plus context, provenance, and family contribution.

It is not generic cloud photo storage, a genealogy database, an AI biography generator, or a public social network.

## Muse boundary

Muse creates space for remembering. Muse may provide a gentle prompt, but it does not invent names, places, dates, relationships, events, motives, or a false consensus. Generated prompts and descriptions remain separate from human testimony. The original human voice remains primary.

## Public agent capability

The public surface helps a person begin. It is intentionally separate from the private archive.

REST:

- `GET /api/v1/product`
- `POST /api/v1/legacy-story-starter`
- `POST /api/v1/interview-plan`
- `POST /api/v1/photo-story-prompts`

MCP:

- `POST /mcp`
- protocol revision `2026-07-28`
- `server/discover`
- `tools/list`
- `tools/call`

Tools:

- `memories.explain_living_memory`
- `memories.create_story_starter`
- `memories.create_interview_plan`
- `memories.create_photo_story_prompts`
- `memories.create_family_story_questions`
- `memories.start_living_memory`

All prompt-generation tools reuse the same deterministic curated prompt library. No model or private archive lookup is required.

## Functional discovery utilities

Ten crawlable utilities are built from a single intent catalog. Each utility immediately calls the same public Legacy Story Starter, so these are multiple discovery doors into one capability rather than separate applications.

- `/questions-to-ask-your-mother`
- `/questions-to-ask-your-father`
- `/questions-to-ask-your-grandmother`
- `/questions-to-ask-your-grandfather`
- `/questions-to-ask-aging-parents`
- `/family-oral-history`
- `/preserving-a-parents-voice`
- `/stories-behind-old-photographs`
- `/family-recipe-stories`
- `/family-reunion-questions`

Every production build emits a Markdown twin at `<utility-path>.md` plus `/discovery-manifest.json`. The manifest contains Story Studio URL templates with `source`, `campaign`, `platform`, and `creative_id` parameters so distributed creatives can land on the matching functional utility instead of a generic homepage.

The utilities accept only coarse prompt-selection settings such as language, relationship category, theme, and time available. They do not request family names or private archive identifiers.

## Privacy boundary

Public agent tools and functional utilities have no code path to authenticated archive/media handlers. They never retrieve or list:

- photographs;
- voice recordings;
- transcripts;
- private Memory Stories;
- family graph or family members;
- ownership records;
- provenance records;
- archive identifiers;
- private share tokens.

Public telemetry records only coarse channel metadata such as tool name, generated starter ID, agent client when supplied, protocol, and success. Request bodies and family-story content are not logged by the public discovery instrumentation.

## Human handoff

A public tool may return a same-origin start URL with non-private source and starter parameters. That URL only opens the ordinary Memories: My Story product. It does not create a private Memory Story, upload media, bind an account, or share anything automatically.

## Languages

The initial deterministic prompt capability supports English and Spanish. It accepts uncertainty and includes phrasing such as “if you remember” rather than asserting family facts.

## Discovery

- `/llms.txt`
- `/llms-full.txt`
- `/openapi.json`
- `/agent/index.md`
- `/agent/capabilities.md`
- `/agent/privacy.md`
- `/agent/evidence.md`
- `/agent/examples.md`
- `/robots.txt`
- `/sitemap.xml`
- `/discovery-manifest.json`

`robots.txt` and `sitemap.xml` are generated from the current request origin because the repository intentionally has no authorized production origin yet. The robots response explicitly allows normal crawlers, `OAI-SearchBot`, and `ChatGPT-User`.
